title: Password and Multi-Factor Authentication Policy
text: All corporate accounts must use passwords of at least 12 characters that combine uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols. Passwords are renewed every 90 days and the last five passwords cannot be reused. After five failed attempts, the account is automatically locked for 30 minutes. Access to the VPN, email, and critical systems requires multi-factor authentication through the approved app. Sharing passwords or storing them in unencrypted documents is prohibited.

title: User Onboarding and Access Assignment Process
text: Human Resources submits the onboarding request for a new employee at least three business days before the start date. The Service Desk creates the email account and network user, and assigns access according to the job profile following the principle of least privilege. The direct manager must approve any additional access to systems or shared folders through a ticket. At the end, the employee signs the asset use responsibility letter and receives their equipment.

title: VPN and Remote Work Policy
text: Remote staff must connect to the corporate network only through the approved VPN with multi-factor authentication. Using public wifi networks without an active VPN is prohibited. The device must have updated antivirus, disk encryption, and automatic screen lock. VPN sessions are closed after eight hours of inactivity. Any connection failure is reported to the Service Desk through a ticket that includes the error message received.

title: Production Change Management Procedure
text: Every change to production systems requires a change request with description, risk, test plan, and rollback plan. The change committee reviews requests every week and approves the maintenance window, which preferably takes place on weekends. Emergency changes are approved by the technology lead and documented within the following 24 hours. After the change is implemented, the service is validated and the request is closed with evidence.

title: Backup and Information Retention Policy
text: Critical servers and databases are backed up every night with incremental copies and every Sunday with a full copy. Backups are stored in an encrypted off-site location and kept for 12 months. The infrastructure team checks the result of backup jobs daily and runs a restore test every quarter. Any failed backup must be logged as an incident and resolved before the next scheduled run.

title: Computer Equipment Request Process
text: Requests for laptops, monitors, and peripherals are logged in the service desk with the job justification and the approval of the direct manager. Procurement validates the budget and selects the equipment from the approved catalog. The estimated delivery time is ten business days. Each device is recorded in the asset inventory with its serial number and owner. The employee must return the previous device for review and secure erasure of its data.

title: Confidential Information Classification and Handling Policy
text: Company information is classified as public, internal, confidential, and restricted. Confidential documents are shared only with authorized staff through folders with controlled permissions and never through personal messaging. Customer data must be encrypted when stored and when transmitted. Department heads review every six months who has access to restricted information. Any unauthorized disclosure is reported immediately to the information security team.

title: Security Incident Response Procedure
text: When a possible security incident occurs, such as phishing, malware, or unauthorized access, the employee must report it immediately to the Service Desk without deleting evidence. The security team classifies the incident by severity, contains the threat by isolating affected devices, investigates the origin, and restores the service. Critical incidents are reported to management within two hours. At closure, the root cause and preventive actions are documented.

title: Employee Offboarding and Access Revocation Process
text: When an employee leaves the company, Human Resources notifies the Service Desk of the departure the same day. The network account, email, VPN, and system access are disabled, and passwords of shared accounts are changed. The computer is collected, the information needed by the successor is backed up, and a secure erasure is performed. The direct manager confirms through a ticket that access was revoked.

title: Authorized Software Installation Policy
text: Only software included in the catalog approved by Technology may be installed on corporate devices. Requests for new software are logged through a ticket with a business justification and are evaluated by security for licensing and risks. Installing pirated programs, unapproved remote access tools, or unknown browser extensions is prohibited. Users do not have local administrator permissions, and software inventory reviews are quarterly.

title: Ticket: User locked out after failed password attempts
text: The user reports being unable to log in to the computer or to email after changing the password this morning. The system shows an account locked message due to too many failed attempts. It was verified in the directory that the account was locked. The account was unlocked, a temporary password was set, and the user was asked to update the password on all mobile devices, since one of them kept trying to connect with the old password.

title: Ticket: VPN will not connect from home, authentication error
text: A remote employee reports that the VPN does not connect and shows an authentication failed error when entering the verification code. It was found that the clock on the laptop was out of sync, which invalidated the code from the multi-factor authentication app. The device time was synchronized, the VPN client was restarted, and the connection was restored. The user was advised to keep automatic time synchronization enabled.

title: Incident: Corporate email server outage
text: For two hours users could not send or receive emails. Monitoring detected that the email service stopped responding because of lack of memory after an update installed the night before. The infrastructure team restarted the service, freed resources, and rolled back the update following the rollback plan. A change request was opened to reschedule the update with additional testing, and users were notified that service was restored.

title: Ticket: Network printer does not print
text: Several users on the second floor report that jobs sent to the network printer stay in the queue and do not print. The printer was checked and a paper jam and an empty toner cartridge were found. In addition, the print server had stuck jobs blocking the queue. The print queue was cleared, the toner was replaced, and a test page printed successfully. Preventive replacement of supplies was scheduled.

title: Incident: ERP system slowness during month-end close
text: During the accounting close, finance users reported very slow response times in the ERP system and in report generation. The analysis showed heavy queries running at the same time on the database and processor usage above 90 percent. Bulk reports were rescheduled outside working hours, indexes were added to the most queried tables, and a capacity review was requested before the next close.

title: Ticket: Suspicious phishing email reported by an employee
text: A sales employee reported an email that pretended to be from the bank and asked her to confirm credentials through a link. She did not click the link and forwarded the message to security. The team analyzed the email, confirmed it was phishing, blocked the sender domain, and deleted the message from other recipients' mailboxes. A notice was sent to the whole company reminding everyone how to identify fraudulent emails and how to report them.

title: Ticket: Laptop will not turn on after a power outage
text: The user reports that the laptop does not turn on after a power outage at the office. The technician checked the charger, the battery, and the charging indicator. It was determined that the power adapter was damaged. A new charger was provided, the device turned on normally, and a disk check ran without errors. The accessory replacement was recorded in the asset inventory and the ticket was closed with the user's confirmation.

title: Incident: Nightly database backup failure
text: The nightly backup job of the main database ended with an error because of lack of space in the destination storage. The infrastructure team freed space by deleting copies that exceeded the retention period and ran the full backup again successfully. The incident was documented, the capacity alert was adjusted to 80 percent, and a restore test was scheduled to verify the integrity of the copy.

title: Ticket: Access denied to a shared folder
text: A procurement analyst cannot open the shared folder of supplier contracts and receives an access denied message. The security group assigned to the user was reviewed and it was confirmed that the permission was missing. With the approval of the direct manager recorded in the ticket, the user was added to the corresponding group with read permissions. The user validated the access and the authorization was documented according to the access assignment process.

title: Incident: Reporting server out of disk space
text: The server that hosts the reporting database stopped accepting new connections because the disk reached 100 percent of its capacity due to the growth of log files. Old logs were compressed and archived, space was freed, and the service was restarted. The storage volume was expanded, automatic log rotation was configured, and capacity alerts were added to prevent the problem from happening again.

title: FAQ: How do I reset my password?
text: If you forgot your password, go to the company self-service portal and select the option to reset it. You will need to confirm your identity with the verification code from the authentication app. The new password must have at least 12 characters with uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols. If your account appears locked because of failed attempts, wait 30 minutes or open a ticket with the Service Desk so they can unlock it.

title: FAQ: How do I connect to the VPN?
text: To connect to the VPN, install the approved client from the software portal, open the application, and enter your network username and password. Then enter the verification code from the multi-factor authentication app. When the status shows connected, you can access the internal systems. If you get an authentication error, check that your device time is synchronized and, if it continues, open a ticket with a screenshot of the error.

title: FAQ: How do I report a suspicious email?
text: If you receive an email from an unknown sender, with strange links, or with urgent requests for personal data or credentials, do not click or download attachments. Use the report phishing button in the email client or forward the message to the security mailbox. The security team will analyze it and let you know the result. If you already entered your credentials, change your password immediately and notify the Service Desk.

title: FAQ: How do I request access to a system or shared folder?
text: To request access to a system or a shared folder, open a ticket with the Service Desk stating the resource, the type of permission needed, and the business justification. Your direct manager will receive a notification to approve the request. Once authorized, the support team assigns the permission within two business days. Temporary access must state the date on which it will be revoked.

title: FAQ: What should I do if I lose my company laptop or phone?
text: If you lose a company device or it is stolen, report it immediately to the Service Desk and to your direct manager, without waiting until the next day. The security team will remotely lock the device, revoke active sessions, and change your passwords. Because disks are encrypted, the risk of information exposure is reduced. You must also file the corresponding report to request a replacement device.

title: Minutes: Monthly security incident review
text: Attendees: security lead, infrastructure, and support. The 14 incidents of the month were reviewed, of which three were phishing attempts and two were account lockouts caused by passwords. It was agreed to strengthen the awareness campaign and to evaluate multi-factor authentication on more systems. The average resolution time dropped from six to four hours. Owners and dates: security will present the training plan in two weeks and support will update the frequently asked questions.

title: Minutes: ERP migration planning
text: Attendees: finance, technology, and the ERP vendor. It was decided to migrate the system to a new version in three phases: testing, pilot with finance, and general go-live. Performance risks during month-end close were identified and it was agreed to carry out the migration outside that period. Technology will present a test and rollback plan, and finance will appoint key users. The tentative go-live date will be confirmed at the change committee.

title: Minutes: Change committee and maintenance window
text: The change committee reviewed five requests. The email server update was approved for Saturday early morning, with a rollback plan and prior testing in a pre-production environment, after the outage caused by the previous update. A database change was rejected for lack of a test plan. It was reminded that all changes must be logged with evidence and that emergency changes are documented within 24 hours.

title: Minutes: Phishing awareness training
text: The annual security training for all staff was planned. The content will include how to identify fraudulent emails, correct password use, multi-factor authentication, and how to report incidents to the Service Desk. Phishing simulations will be run every quarter to measure how many users click suspicious links. Human Resources will follow up on attendance and security will present the results to management.

title: Minutes: Storage capacity and backup review
text: Infrastructure presented storage growth: log files and databases increased by 30 percent during the year. After the lack-of-space incidents on the reporting server and on the backup destination, it was agreed to expand capacity, automate log rotation, and configure alerts at 80 percent. A quarterly backup restore test was also scheduled and retention periods will be reviewed.

title: Acceptable Use of Email and Messaging Policy
text: Corporate email and the approved messaging platform must be used only for work purposes. Employees must not forward internal or confidential information to personal accounts or send it through unapproved messaging apps. Attachments larger than 25 MB must be shared through the corporate cloud storage with controlled permissions. Chain messages, unsolicited mass mailing, and automatic forwarding rules to external addresses are prohibited. Suspicious messages must be reported with the report phishing button.

title: Mobile Device and Bring Your Own Device Policy
text: Personal or company phones and tablets that access corporate email or applications must be enrolled in the mobile device management platform. Enrolled devices require a screen lock PIN, encryption, and the latest operating system update. The company can remotely wipe only the corporate workspace of a personal device. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the Service Desk immediately so access can be revoked and the multi-factor authentication app can be moved to a new phone.

title: Security Patch and Update Management Procedure
text: Operating system and application security patches are evaluated every month by the infrastructure team. Critical patches are installed within 72 hours on servers and workstations after testing in a pre-production environment. Updates to production servers follow the change management procedure and are applied in the approved maintenance window with a rollback plan. Workstations restart automatically on Friday night to complete pending updates, and compliance is reported to management every quarter.

title: Cloud Storage and File Sharing Policy
text: Work files must be stored in the corporate cloud storage, which is backed up and encrypted, instead of on the local disk. Files can be shared with external partners only through links with an expiration date and a password. Confidential and restricted files cannot be shared externally without approval from the department head. Deleted files can be recovered by the owner from the recycle bin for 30 days. Personal cloud storage services cannot be used for company information.

title: Service Desk Ticket Prioritization and Service Level Procedure
text: Every request or incident is logged as a ticket in the service desk and classified by impact and urgency. Critical priority tickets, such as an outage affecting a whole area, have a response time of 30 minutes and a resolution target of four hours. High priority tickets are resolved within one business day, and normal requests within three business days. Tickets that exceed the service level are escalated to the support lead, and the user confirms the solution before the ticket is closed.

title: Ticket: Authentication app not working on a new phone
text: The user changed phones over the weekend and can no longer receive the verification codes, so she cannot access the VPN or email from outside the office. The multi-factor authentication app was still registered on the old phone. After confirming her identity with her manager, support removed the old registration, enrolled the new phone in the mobile device management platform, and registered the authentication app again. Access was restored and the user received the guide for future phone changes.

title: Incident: Malware detected on a sales workstation
text: The antivirus console generated a high severity alert for malware on a workstation in the sales area. The device was isolated from the network to contain the threat and the user's password was changed as a precaution. The analysis showed that the malicious file came from an attachment in an email that pretended to be an invoice. The disk was cleaned and the operating system was reinstalled from a secure image. The phishing indicators were blocked and the incident was reviewed at the monthly security meeting.

title: Ticket: No audio in video conference meetings
text: A manager reports that other participants cannot hear him in video conference meetings, although he can hear them. The technician found that the laptop was using the internal microphone, which was disabled in the privacy settings after a system update. The microphone permission was enabled for the meeting application, the headset was selected as the default device, and a test call was made successfully. The user was shown how to check audio settings before a meeting.

title: Ticket: Software installation blocked by administrator permissions
text: An analyst tried to install a data visualization program downloaded from the internet and received a message asking for administrator credentials. Users do not have local administrator permissions, and the program was not in the approved software catalog. The request was redirected through a ticket with the business justification, and security evaluated the license and risks. Once approved, the program was added to the catalog and installed from the software portal.

title: Incident: Wireless network outage on the third floor
text: Users on the third floor lost the wireless connection and could not access internal systems or video conference meetings for one hour. The network team found that one access point had failed after a firmware update and the others could not handle the load. The update was rolled back, the failed access point was replaced, and the connection was restored. A change request was created to update the firmware during the maintenance window with prior testing.

title: FAQ: How do I set up the authentication app on a new phone?
text: Before changing phones, open a ticket with the Service Desk so they can remove the registration of the old device. Install the approved authentication app on the new phone, enroll it in the mobile device management platform, and scan the registration code that you will receive by email. Test the code by signing in to the self-service portal. If you already lost the old phone, report it immediately so your access can be protected.

title: FAQ: How do I request a new laptop or monitor?
text: Open a request in the service desk, choose the equipment from the approved catalog, and write the job justification. Your direct manager will receive a notification to approve it, and procurement will validate the budget. Delivery usually takes ten business days. When you receive the new laptop, you must return the previous one so the support team can back up your information and perform a secure erasure.

title: FAQ: How do I install approved software?
text: Open the software portal on your corporate computer and search for the program in the approved catalog. Select install and the program will be installed automatically without administrator permissions. If the program you need is not in the catalog, open a ticket with the business justification so security can evaluate its license and risks. Do not download programs from the internet or install browser extensions that are not approved.

title: FAQ: How do I share confidential files securely?
text: Save the file in the corporate cloud storage and share it only with the people who need it, using controlled permissions. For external partners, create a link with an expiration date and a password, and send the password through a different channel. Never send confidential information through personal email or messaging apps. If the file is classified as restricted, ask for approval from your department head before sharing it.

title: FAQ: How do I recover a deleted or overwritten file?
text: If you deleted a file from the corporate cloud storage, open the recycle bin and restore it within 30 days. To recover a previous version of an overwritten file, open the version history and select the date you need. If the file was on a shared server or is older than 30 days, open a ticket with the Service Desk stating the path and the approximate date so the infrastructure team can restore it from the backup.

title: FAQ: How long will it take to solve my ticket?
text: Resolution time depends on the priority of the ticket. Critical incidents that affect a whole area are attended within 30 minutes and resolved within four hours. High priority tickets are resolved within one business day, and normal requests within three business days. You can check the status of your ticket in the self-service portal. If the time is exceeded, the ticket is escalated automatically to the support lead.

title: FAQ: How do I connect to the office wireless network?
text: Select the corporate wireless network on your laptop and sign in with your network username and password. Your device must have the company certificate, which is installed automatically on corporate laptops. Visitors must use the guest network with the daily code provided at reception, which does not give access to internal systems. If the connection fails on a whole floor, report it to the Service Desk as an incident.

title: FAQ: What can I do if the printer does not print?
text: First check that you selected the correct network printer and that it shows no paper jam or toner warning on its screen. Cancel your job in the print queue and send it again. If several people cannot print, the print server may have stuck jobs, so open a ticket with the Service Desk indicating the printer name and the floor. Do not try to open the printer to remove internal parts.

title: FAQ: What happens on my first day at the company?
text: On your first day, the Service Desk will give you your laptop, your network user, and your email account, which were created during the onboarding process. You will set your password, register the authentication app on your phone, and sign the asset use responsibility letter. Your manager will request any additional access you need through a ticket. During the first week you must complete the security awareness training.

title: FAQ: How do I report a security incident?
text: If you notice something unusual, such as a virus alert, a suspicious email, files that changed without reason, or an unknown login to your account, report it immediately to the Service Desk. Do not turn off the device or delete evidence, but disconnect it from the network if the security team asks you to. Describe what happened and when. The security team will classify the incident by severity and keep you informed.

title: Minutes: Service Desk monthly performance review
text: Attendees: support lead, service desk analysts, and the operations manager. In the month, 412 tickets were registered and 91 percent were resolved within the service level. The most frequent requests were password resets, account lockouts, and access to shared folders. It was agreed to promote the self-service password reset portal and to publish new frequently asked questions. Owners and dates: the support lead will present the escalation report next month.

title: Minutes: Onboarding process improvement meeting
text: Attendees: Human Resources, Service Desk, and procurement. Three new employees started without a laptop because the onboarding request arrived one day before the start date. It was agreed that Human Resources will submit requests at least five business days in advance and that procurement will keep a stock of preconfigured laptops. The access profiles by job will be reviewed to apply least privilege. Support will update the first day guide.

title: Minutes: Monthly patch compliance review
text: Attendees: infrastructure, security, and support. Patch compliance reached 94 percent on workstations and 88 percent on servers. Two servers could not be updated because the vendor application was not compatible, so a temporary exception with additional monitoring was approved. It was agreed to test critical patches in pre-production within 48 hours and to include server updates in the next maintenance window approved by the change committee.

title: Minutes: Approval of the mobile device policy
text: Attendees: security lead, legal, Human Resources, and technology. The bring your own device policy was reviewed and approved. Employees who want corporate email on their personal phone must enroll it in the mobile device management platform, which only controls the corporate workspace. Legal confirmed that the remote wipe will not affect personal data. Human Resources will communicate the policy, and support will enroll devices during the next two months.

title: Minutes: Cloud storage migration kickoff
text: Attendees: technology, security, and department representatives. It was decided to move shared folders from the file server to the corporate cloud storage in four waves by department. Security presented the rules to share files with external partners using links with expiration dates. Each department will clean obsolete files before the migration. The infrastructure team will keep the file server in read only mode for one month as a backup.

title: Minutes: Disaster recovery drill results
text: Attendees: infrastructure, security, and the operations manager. The annual disaster recovery drill simulated the loss of the main data center. The ERP database and email were restored from off-site backups in five hours, one hour above the target. The delay was caused by an outdated restore procedure. It was agreed to update the procedure, automate the restore of critical servers, and repeat the restore test of the database next quarter.

title: Minutes: Annual software license audit
text: Attendees: technology, procurement, and finance. The software inventory showed 40 unused licenses of a design program and six computers with unapproved programs installed. It was agreed to recover the unused licenses, uninstall the unapproved software, and remind staff of the authorized software installation policy. Procurement will negotiate the renewal of the office suite, and security will review the software catalog every quarter.

title: Minutes: Wireless network upgrade planning
text: Attendees: network team, infrastructure, and facilities. After the outage on the third floor, the condition of the access points was reviewed and it was found that half of them are more than six years old. It was approved to replace the access points in phases, starting with the floors with more video conference meetings. Each phase will be scheduled in the maintenance window through the change committee, with firmware tests in a lab.

title: Minutes: Knowledge base improvement meeting
text: Attendees: support lead, service desk analysts, and the knowledge management team. It was found that 35 percent of tickets ask questions already answered in existing guides that users could not find. It was agreed to publish frequently asked questions for the most common requests, link each closed ticket to the related policy, and test a document recommender and a chatbot that answers questions using the knowledge base.

title: Minutes: ERP go-live retrospective
text: Attendees: finance, technology, and the ERP vendor. The new ERP version went live after the pilot with finance. Response times improved by 40 percent during the month-end close thanks to the new database indexes. Two incidents with report generation were solved in the first week. It was agreed to document the known errors as frequently asked questions, train key users from other areas, and close the change request with evidence.
